source.shape_note: One row per (window, claimed caller). A system emitting one row per window with several caller columns is a different shape and needs its own profile; guessing at a universal reshaper here would silently mis-associate scores with callers.
source.tool_independence: This profile names roles, never vendor columns. Any attribution system reaches VAWLUME through the same declaration by pointing each role at whatever it happened to call it.

context.timing_note: Imported window times are NATIVE to the exporting system's own clock and are stored unchanged. Whether that clock is the recording's clock is a question this profile cannot answer and does not try to: relating it to a VAWLUME event is correspondence work, and it happens after intake with an explicit transform.

native_window_id.note: The exporting system's own window identifier, stored verbatim. It is never interpreted as a VAWLUME detection ID even when it looks like one.

caller_label.note: The exporting system's label for the claimed caller, stored verbatim. It becomes a VAWLUME entity only through caller_label_resolution below.

score.note: Optional. Unconstrained range. Stored exactly as the file carries it.

probability.note: Optional. Must lie in [0,1]. A value outside that range is refused rather than clamped, because clamping would silently rewrite the exporter's claim.

value_semantics.score: Exporting-system caller score; producer declared in context.exporting_system; range as the exporter defines it; uncalibrated; not a probability and not comparable across exporting systems
value_semantics.probability: Exporting-system caller probability; producer declared in context.exporting_system; range=[0,1]; calibration is the exporter's claim and is not validated by VAWLUME
value_semantics.semantics_note: These strings travel with every stored number. They say what the number meant WHERE IT CAME FROM. VAWLUME neither recomputes nor re-normalizes them, because a rescaled imported score is unauditable forever: the original is gone.

caller_label_resolution.policy_note: A label in somebody else's file is a string. VAWLUME never infers which entity it denotes from string similarity, case folding, or edit distance, and never creates an entity to accommodate an unrecognized label. Every label is declared here or the import is refused by name.
caller_label_resolution.unresolved_label_note: An imported label naming an animal not among the run's participating entities is a surfaced problem, not a new entity. The import names every offending label rather than dropping those rows.

mapping_policy.preserve_source_values_note: No rescaling, no renormalization, no clamping, and no conversion of a score into a probability because it happened to fall in [0,1].
mapping_policy.unmappable_row_note: A row that cannot be mapped is reported as an issue and excluded from the plan. It is never silently dropped, because a preview that hides what it could not read is worse than one that reads nothing.
mapping_policy.correspondence_note: Intake relates imported windows to nothing. Associating them with VAWLUME detections or consensus events is a separate, explicit step with its own eligibility rule.

correspondence.rule_note: This asks whether an imported attribution claim refers to a call VAWLUME knows about. That is a different question from whether two detectors found the same call, and it is deliberately NOT the matching specification's rule: a detector disagreeing with another detector is a measurement difference, while an attribution system's window disagreeing with a VAWLUME event may mean the systems were segmenting different things entirely.
correspondence.min_temporal_iou_note: Deliberately independent of the matching specification's floor, and deliberately lower than it. An attribution system's window often brackets a call loosely, because it was produced to localize a caller rather than to delimit a vocalization, so a floor tuned for detector-to-detector agreement would discard true correspondences whose only fault is a generous window. The two floors happening to coincide would be a coincidence, not a shared calibration, and neither layer may be tuned by changing the other.
correspondence.preserve_ambiguity_note: A window plausibly referring to two VAWLUME events produces two correspondences, both stored with their scores. Nothing chooses. A correspondence layer that picked a winner would destroy the evidence a later reviewer needs, and the reviewer is the only one who can weigh it.
correspondence.calibration_note: min_temporal_iou is a demonstration value chosen to exercise behaviour on synthetic windows. It is not calibrated, and no correspondence produced under it is validated.

validation.require_one_of_score_or_probability_note: A label with no number is a legitimate import. The writer records NULL for both, never 1.0: converting a name into certainty is the specific failure this refuses.
